variables.name: STUDYID
variables.label: Study Identifier
variables.description: Unique identifier for a study.

variables.name: DOMAIN
variables.label: Domain Abbreviation
variables.description: Two-character abbreviation for the domain.

variables.name: USUBJID
variables.label: Unique Subject Identifier
variables.description: Identifier used to uniquely identify a subject across all studies for all applications or submissions involving the product.

variables.name: SUSEQ
variables.label: Sequence Number
variables.description: Sequence number given to ensure uniqueness of subject records within a domain. May be any valid number.

variables.name: SUGRPID
variables.label: Group ID
variables.description: Used to tie together a block of related records in a single domain for a subject.

variables.name: SUSPID
variables.label: Sponsor-Defined Identifier
variables.description: Sponsor-defined reference number. May be preprinted on the CRF as an explicit line identifier or defined in the sponsor's operational database. Example: Line number on a Tobacco & Alcohol Use CRF page.

variables.name: SUTRT
variables.label: Reported Name of Substance
variables.description: Substance name. Examples: "CIGARETTES", "COFFEE".

variables.name: SUMODIFY
variables.label: Modified Substance Name
variables.description: If SUTRT is modified, then the modified text is placed here.

variables.name: SUDECOD
variables.label: Standardized Substance Name
variables.description: Standardized or dictionary-derived text description of SUTRT or SUMODIFY if the sponsor chooses to code the substance use. The sponsor is expected to provide the dictionary name and version used to map the terms utilizing the external codelist element in the Define-XML document.

variables.name: SUCAT
variables.label: Category for Substance Use
variables.description: Used to define a category of related records. Examples: "TOBACCO", "ALCOHOL", or "CAFFEINE".

variables.name: SUSCAT
variables.label: Subcategory for Substance Use
variables.description: A further categorization of substance use. Examples: "CIGARS", "CIGARETTES", "BEER", "WINE".

variables.name: SUPRESP
variables.label: SU Pre-Specified
variables.codelist: Version-agnostic anchor resource for codelist C66742
variables.description: Used to indicate whether ("Y"/null) information about the use of a specific substance was solicited on the CRF.

variables.name: SUOCCUR
variables.label: SU Occurrence
variables.codelist: Version-agnostic anchor resource for codelist C66742
variables.description: When the use of specific substances is solicited, SUOCCUR is used to indicate whether ("Y"/"N") a particular prespecified substance was used. Values are null for substances not specifically solicited.

variables.name: SUSTAT
variables.label: Completion Status
variables.codelist: Version-agnostic anchor resource for codelist C66789
variables.description: When the use of prespecified substances is solicited, the completion status indicates that there was no response to the question about the prespecified substance. When there is no prespecified list on the CRF, then the completion status indicates that substance use was not assessed for the subject.

variables.name: SUREASND
variables.label: Reason Substance Use Not Collected
variables.description: Describes the reason substance use was not collected. Used in conjunction with SUSTAT when value of SUSTAT is "NOT DONE".

variables.name: SUCLAS
variables.label: Substance Use Class
variables.description: Substance use class. May be obtained from coding. When coding to a single class, populate with class value. If using a dictionary and coding to multiple classes, then follow Section 4.2.8.3, Multiple Values for a Non-result Qualifier Variable, or omit SUCLAS.

variables.name: SUCLASCD
variables.label: Substance Use Class Code
variables.description: Code corresponding to SUCLAS. May be obtained from coding.

variables.name: SUDOSE
variables.label: Substance Use Consumption
variables.description: Amount of SUTRT consumed. Not populated if SUDOSTXT is populated.

variables.name: SUDOSTXT
variables.label: Substance Use Consumption Text
variables.description: Substance use consumption amounts or a range of consumption information collected in text form. Not populated if SUDOSE is populated.

variables.name: SUDOSU
variables.label: Consumption Units
variables.codelist: Version-agnostic anchor resource for codelist C71620
variables.description: Units for SUDOSE, SUDOSTOT, or SUDOSTXT. Examples: "oz", "CIGARETTE", "PACK", "g".

variables.name: SUDOSFRM
variables.label: Dose Form
variables.codelist: Version-agnostic anchor resource for codelist C66726
variables.description: Dose form for SUTRT. Examples: "INJECTABLE", "LIQUID", "POWDER".

variables.name: SUDOSFRQ
variables.label: Use Frequency Per Interval
variables.codelist: Version-agnostic anchor resource for codelist C71113
variables.description: Usually expressed as the number of repeated administrations of SUDOSE within a specific time period. Example: "Q24H" (every day).

variables.name: SUDOSTOT
variables.label: Total Daily Consumption
variables.description: Total daily use of SUTRT using the units in SUDOSU. Used when dosing is collected as total daily dose. If a sponsor needs to aggregate the data over a period other than daily, then the aggregated total could be recorded in a supplemental qualifier variable.

variables.name: SUROUTE
variables.label: Route of Administration
variables.codelist: Version-agnostic anchor resource for codelist C66729
variables.description: Route of administration for SUTRT. Examples: "ORAL", "INTRAVENOUS".

variables.name: TAETORD
variables.label: Planned Order of Element within Arm
variables.description: Number that gives the planned order of the element within the arm for the element in which the substance use started. Null for substances that started before study participation.

variables.name: EPOCH
variables.label: Epoch
variables.codelist: Version-agnostic anchor resource for codelist C99079
variables.description: Epoch associated with the start date/time of the substance use. Null for substances that started before study participation.

variables.name: SUSTDTC
variables.label: Start Date/Time of Substance Use
variables.description: Start date/time of the substance use represented in ISO 8601 character format.

variables.name: SUENDTC
variables.label: End Date/Time of Substance Use
variables.description: End date/time of the substance use represented in ISO 8601 character format.

variables.name: SUSTDY
variables.label: Study Day of Start of Substance Use
variables.description: Study day of start of substance use relative to the sponsor-defined RFSTDTC.

variables.name: SUENDY
variables.label: Study Day of End of Substance Use
variables.description: Study day of end of substance use relative to the sponsor-defined RFSTDTC.

variables.name: SUDUR
variables.label: Duration of Substance Use
variables.description: Collected duration of substance use in ISO 8601 format. Used only if collected on the CRF and not derived from start and end date/times.

variables.name: SUSTRF
variables.label: Start Relative to Reference Period
variables.codelist: Version-agnostic anchor resource for codelist C66728
variables.description: Describes the start of the substance use relative to the sponsor-defined reference period. The sponsor-defined reference period is a continuous period of time defined by a discrete starting point and a discrete ending point (represented by RFSTDTC and RFENDTC in Demographics). If information such as "PRIOR" was collected, this information may be translated into SUSTRF. \n Not all values of the codelist are allowable for this variable. See Section 4.4.7, Use of Relative Timing Variables.

variables.name: SUENRF
variables.label: End Relative to Reference Period
variables.codelist: Version-agnostic anchor resource for codelist C66728
variables.description: Describes the end of the substance use with relative to the sponsor-defined reference period. The sponsor-defined reference period is a continuous period of time defined by a discrete starting point and a discrete ending point (represented by RFSTDTC and RFENDTC in Demographics). If information such as "PRIOR", "ONGOING", or "CONTINUING" was collected, this information may be translated into SUENRF. \n Not all values of the codelist are allowable for this variable. See Section 4.4.7, Use of Relative Timing Variables.

variables.name: SUSTRTPT
variables.label: Start Relative to Reference Time Point
variables.codelist: Version-agnostic anchor resource for codelist C66728
variables.description: Identifies the start of the substance as being before or after the reference time point defined by variable SUSTTPT. \n Not all values of the codelist are allowable for this variable. See Section 4.4.7 , Use of Relative Timing Variables.

variables.name: SUSTTPT
variables.label: Start Reference Time Point
variables.description: Description or date/time in ISO 8601 character format of the reference point referred to by SUSTRTPT. Examples: "2003-12-15", "VISIT 1".

variables.name: SUENRTPT
variables.label: End Relative to Reference Time Point
variables.codelist: Version-agnostic anchor resource for codelist C66728
variables.description: Identifies the end of the substance as being before or after the reference time point defined by variable SUENTPT. \n Not all values of the codelist are allowable for this variable. See Section 4.4.7 , Use of Relative Timing Variables.

variables.name: SUENTPT
variables.label: End Reference Time Point
variables.description: Description or date/time in ISO 8601 character format of the reference point referred to by SUENRTPT. Examples: "2003-12-25", "VISIT 2".
